content: Azlocillin is an acylampicillin antibiotic that possesses an extended spectrum of antibacterial activity. It demonstrates greater in vitro potency compared to carboxypenicillins. Azlocillin shares similarities with other antibiotics such as mezlocillin and piperacillin. This antibiotic exhibits efficacy against a wide range of bacterial species, including Pseudomonas aeruginosa. Notably, unlike most cephalosporins, azlocillin also shows activity against Enterococci. Azlocillin is classified as a broad-spectrum antibiotic, effective against both Gram-positive and Gram-negative bacteria. The following are the minimum inhibitory concentration (MIC) susceptibility ranges for certain clinically significant organisms: Escherichia coli: 1 μg/mL to 32 μg/mL Haemophilus species: Data not fully provided in the excerpt.
